page: Amazon Web Services c6in.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in single-core operations, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1518.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show limitations. The multi-core stress-ng score of 3853.28 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3252.0 fall into the weaker performance brackets. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large block read-only speeds at 29.04 GB/sec and write speeds at 22.17 GB/sec. Despite these memory bottlenecks, the instance maintains average throughput in static web serving at 6.49 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 27.68 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6in.xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile suitable for network-optimized and compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. Given the 1:2 resource density and average single-threaded performance, this instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, basic network appliances, and moderate utility computing workloads.
